known_limitations: AT-1620/1622 bit-exact GPU correctness (coopmat): requires NVIDIA hardware with CooperativeMatrixKHR — cannot validate on Lavapipe (CoopMatUnsupported). Tests are #[ignore]-gated per spec.
AT-1630 bit-exact GPU: requires real GPU (Lavapipe should work for pure f32 attention). Test is #[ignore]-gated.
AT-1710 TFLOPS: requires NVIDIA GPU + AXC_ENABLE_GPU_BENCHES=1. QA must measure and fill <__TFLOPS__> / <__PCT__> placeholders in DESIGN.md §3.1.15 + ROADMAP.md.
AT-1706c scalar→coopmat non-rejection: pre-existing latent gap (Let path has the same behavior). Not a M3.3-introduced regression. Test documents it honestly.

The `_dummy = inner;` pattern in AT-1704d test compiles but is semantically meaningless — used to avoid f16 scalar limitation while testing the non-descend behavior. Correct behavior is proven by the absence of the LoopCarriedCoopMatAcrossBreakUnsupported error.
deviations: PART C exp: kept Taylor approximation (1+x+x²/2) instead of exp2-based OpExtInst GLSL.std.450. The spec said RECOMMENDED (not mandatory) for exp2; Taylor is simpler (no mathfn.rs/ext-inst-import needed) and the CPU reference uses the IDENTICAL formula. This deviation is documented in tiled_attention.axc comments and DESIGN.md §3.1.15.

matmul_shared_coopmat.axc fixture is M=N=16, N_SIZE in AT-1620 test is 24 (non-symmetric). The coopmat tile itself is 16x16; the non-symmetric N_SIZE means tile_col=0,1 map to different C positions. The GPU fixture for single-workgroup dispatch uses N=16 (K=32) in the current AT-1620 body to keep it simple — the K=2*tile_k non-symmetry is the LOAD-BEARING fixture (not the M/N asymmetry). If QA finds the fixture confusing, it can be adjusted to M=N_SIZE=16, K=32 trivially.
